question: Should point-in-time QA be scored on answer content, on citation validity, or both, and which definition determines whether version contamination counts as a user-visible failure?
description: The size of the measured harm depends on how correctness is defined. Scoring answer content only makes contamination appear benign whenever a superseded clause yields the same answer; scoring citation validity counts an out-of-force provision as a failure even when the answer matches. The literature treats anachronistic citation as a defect while the point-in-time system reports answer accuracy as its headline, so the field has not settled which definition governs. If content-only scoring is required, the contribution's practical significance rests on the subset where answers actually differ.
confidence_basis: Verified precedents show both outcome types reported side by side, and the two definitions provably differ in sensitivity, so the claim-matched design follows from the evidence rather than from preference; only the magnitudes remain unmeasured.
rationale: This construct choice directly sets the measured harm and therefore the practical significance of the benchmark; plan E009 deliberately separates the two scorings so the choice can be made on evidence rather than assumed.
resolution: Resolved as a claim-matched dual-scoring rule rather than a choice of one definition. Retrieval-level claims are scored by version identity - whether the returned passage was in force at the target date - following the criterion legal analysis prescribes and the temporal-validity encoding of legal benchmarks, because content scoring is blind to contamination when successive versions share wording. End-to-end claims are scored by answer accuracy restricted to the answer-differential stratum, because only there can a wrong version change the answer; citation-validity failure and the screen pass rate are reported alongside, and no single aggregate is used. Prior work supports this separation: a point-in-time system headlines answer accuracy while reporting temporal evidence leakage separately, and legal analysis treats anachronistic citation as the characteristic failure. The rule is now embedded in modification M005 and plan E009, with the pre-registration requirement that each metric be tied in advance to the claim it adjudicates. A residual definitional case - versions whose text is unchanged - is recorded separately as U040.
